question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 1 \\ -1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 1 \\ -1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(1-\lambda )+1\cdot 1 & =0 \\ 3-3\lambda -\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +4 & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $A$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation.
